subject: Audit export and retention clarifications for RFP - Helix Health
messages:
From: Ops - Helix Health <ops@helixhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - Helix Health <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit export / retention details for RFP - Helix Health

Mina,

Thanks for taking the Helix RFP. A few specific items our Ops and Legal teams want to confirm for the audit log/retention section. We need short, concrete answers we can include in the RFP appendix:

- Supported export formats (NDJSON, Parquet, Avro, others?) and whether exports preserve event schema and per-event metadata (trace ids, route, model_version).
- Bulk export delivery options: presigned S3, direct push to our S3/GCS, streaming to a Kafka topic, or timeboxed download bundles.
- Time-to-deliver SLA for a full export of 90 days of audit events (rough estimate in hours for typical dataset sizes).
- Tamper-evidence: do exports include signed manifests (SHA256) and an export audit trail linking job IDs back to the system logs? Are manifests signed by an HSM or similar?
- Retention controls: can retention be configured per-route or per-customer? Can we set legal-hold to freeze deletion for specific datasets? How are retention overrides governed (role approvals / written request)?
- Redaction/PII: options for at-export redaction vs. in-place redaction; support for deterministic vs. probabilistic redaction; whether redaction can be applied at field-level during export.
- Chain-of-custody: do you produce delivery receipts, MD5/SHA checksums, and an access log showing who downloaded or received an export?

Attachments: none on our side yet. If you can provide a single-page export spec and a sample manifest example that shows timestamp/provenance and checksums, that would be ideal.

We'd like a written response we can include in the RFP by EOD Tuesday (US PST). If helpful, propose a 30-min tech sync.

Thanks,
Alex Park
Ops Manager, Helix Health
ops@helixhealth.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Ops - Helix Health <ops@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Legal - Helix Health <legal@helixhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit export / retention details for RFP - Helix Health

Alex — thanks, appreciate the focused list. High-level answers below; Ben and I will follow with a technical appendix and a sample manifest. I've attached a one-page overview (redwood-audit-export-overview.pdf) for your RFP appendix.

- Formats: NDJSON and Parquet are first-class; Avro and CSV available on request. All formats include per-event metadata (request_id, model_version, route, tenant_id) and event-level timestamps.
- Delivery: presigned S3 URLs (preferred), direct push to customer S3 (cross-account role), and SFTP are supported. Streaming to Kafka is supported for Dedicated customers via a connector.
- SLA: Typical bulk export of ~90 days (100–200M events) is staged and delivered within 24–72 hours depending on size and retention tier. We provide a sizing estimate once we see the event rate and avg event size.
- Tamper evidence: Exports include a job-level signed manifest with SHA256 checksums for each bundle and an export job audit entry referencing internal job_id and operator. Manifests can be signed using our KMS-backed signing key; we can arrange HSM-backed signatures for enterprise contracts.
- Retention: Retention policies can be set per-tenant and per-route. Legal hold is available and will freeze deletions for specified datasets; overrides require written approval from an authorized security contact per the contract.
- Redaction: Support for field-level redaction applied during export (configurable allowlist/denylist and deterministic hashing). We also offer in-platform redaction workflows for stored logs.
- Chain-of-custody: Delivery receipts, job IDs, and access logs are produced. We include timestamps and operator IDs; download events are recorded and available in the console and as a separate export.

We'll attach the export spec and a sample manifest with checksums in a follow-up. Can you confirm what S3 bucket pattern/ARN you'll want the presigned uploads to use and whether Helix requires HSM-signed manifests by default?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-audit-export-overview.pdf (application/pdf, 225 KB stub)

From: Legal - Helix Health <legal@helixhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 14:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit export / retention details for RFP - Helix Health

Mina — quick legal clarifications that must be explicit in the RFP response:

1) Immutability evidence: for any export marked as "immutability preserved" we require (a) manifest of per-file SHA256 checksums, (b) a signed export manifest with signing key metadata, (c) a timestamp provenance chain (UTC + NTP source if possible).
2) Legal hold procedures: we need the exact steps and SLAs to place a legal hold, including who can request it, how it's acknowledged, and audit evidence that prevents deletion.
3) Tamper detection: are manifests verifiable independently by Helix using a public key or JWK, or is verification only internal? We prefer a public verifiable signature.
4) Export integrity in-transit: confirm TLS versions and support for server-side and client-side encryption on delivered bundles.

Please be explicit — we will include the wording verbatim in the contract SOW.

Regards,
Tara Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Helix Health
legal@helixhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tara Nguyen <legal@helixhealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Alex Park <ops@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit export / retention details for RFP - Helix Health

Tara / Alex — diving into the technical specifics you asked for. Inline answers and an example manifest excerpt below.

1) Immutability evidence
- We produce a per-export job manifest that lists file names, object sizes, SHA256 checksums, creation timestamps, and the Redwood export_job_id.
- Signing: enterprise contracts can require HSM-backed signing via customer-approved KMS (we support AWS CloudHSM-backed keys or on-prem HSM integration). The manifest includes the signing key fingerprint and a signature block in detached JWS format so you can independently verify via the public JWK.
- Example manifest line (NDJSON bundle): {"file":"audit-202604-0001.ndjson.gz", "size":1234567, "sha256":"3a7bd3...9f2c", "created_at":"2026-06-17T14:03:21Z"} (we will provide a full sample in the attachment).

2) Legal hold workflows
- Request: holder (Helix security or legal) submits a legal-hold request via the Console or API with justification and target dataset (tenant, route, time window).
- Acknowledgement: automated acknowledgement email + system ticket with an immutable record of the request.
- Enforcement: retention engine marks objects as "preserved" and prevents scheduled deletion.
- Overrides: only authorized Redwood Security leadership (named in SOW) can approve an override, and such requests generate an auditable approval record. Standard SLA for acknowledgement is 4 business hours; enforcement is immediate once request is validated.

3) Tamper detection & verification
- Public verification: manifests are signed and we can publish the corresponding JWK (or provide it to Helix) so you can independently verify signatures.
- Checksums: we use SHA256 for integrity and include a manifest-level hash (Merkle root for very large bundles available on request).

4) In-transit & at-rest encryption
- All exports use TLS1.2+ for transfer; we support TLS1.3.
- Delivery options: presigned S3 uploads will use server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) according to your bucket policy; client-side encryption workflows are supported if you require customer-managed keys.

5) Formats & schema
- NDJSON: preserves event-per-line with metadata fields (request_id, user_id, tenant_id, model_version, route, trace_id).
- Parquet: columnar for efficient analytics; includes the same metadata in schema columns.
- We include a versioned schema file with each export; schema evolution is handled with minor/major version tags.

6) Delivery timelines & QA
- Small exports (<50M events): typically 12–24 hours.
- Medium (50–500M): 24–72 hours.
- Large (>500M): 72+ hours, with streaming handoff options. We will provide a precise estimate after a sizing call.

Attachments: export_spec_sheet.csv (contains sample file naming, compression, and manifest schema), sample-manifest-sha256.txt (detached signature example).

If Helix would like, we can schedule a 45-min validation exercise where we run a sample export of a synthetic 7-day window into a Helix test bucket so you can verify checksums and signature verification.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: export_spec_sheet.csv (text/csv, 12 KB stub), sample-manifest-sha256.txt (text/plain, 2 KB stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Ops - Helix Health <ops@helixhealth.com>, Legal - Helix Health <legal@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit export / retention clarifications for RFP - Helix Health

Thanks Tara / Alex — summarizing the agreed wording you can drop into the SOW / RFP appendix (verbatim-friendly):

- Redwood will provide exports in NDJSON and Parquet formats (Avro/CSV on request). Exports preserve per-event metadata (request_id, tenant_id, model_version, route, trace_id).
- Delivery options include presigned S3 uploads (cross-account), direct push to customer buckets, and SFTP. TLS1.2+ (TLS1.3 recommended) is used for in-transit encryption; server-side or client-side encryption can be used per customer policy.
- Tamper evidence: each export includes a detached signed manifest containing per-file SHA256 checksums, object sizes, and creation timestamps. Manifests are signed using a KMS-backed key; enterprise agreements can specify HSM-backed signing. Public JWKs or an exchangeable verification key will be provided to Helix for independent signature verification.
- Retention: retention windows are configurable per-tenant and per-route. Legal holds can be requested via the Console or API; requests are acknowledged within 4 business hours and enforcement is immediate. Override of a legal hold requires written authorization from named Redwood Security leadership.
- SLA estimates for bulk export: ~12–24 hours for small, 24–72 hours for medium, 72+ for very large datasets. A sizing call will produce a firm delivery SLA.

Next steps: Ben and I can run the sample export into your test bucket next week (we need the test S3 ARN and an IAM role or presigned policy). Can Helix confirm a test-bucket ARN and whether you want an HSM-signed manifest by default?

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ops - Helix Health <ops@helixhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - Helix Health <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Audit export / retention clarifications for RFP - Helix Health

Mina — thanks, that wording is perfect for the RFP. We'll take the paragraph verbatim. Test-bucket: arn:aws:s3:::helix-rdwr-test-exports. We'll provide a cross-account role and a short-lived presigned policy.

We want HSM-signed manifests by default for Helix production exports; for the sample export into the test bucket you can use KMS-backed signing if HSM isn't provisioned yet. Please schedule the sample export for next Wednesday (23 Jun) morning PT.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — I'll follow up with the role and S3 details.

- Alex
Ops Manager, Helix Health
